title: Linearisation, ctrb/obsv, PID design, delays
description:
Linear analysis of the TVC rocket about 9 operating points on the nominal boost, from rail exit to the start of the thrust tail-off, where TVC authority ends. Linearisation is numeric, by finite differences straight through the 6-DOF dynamics, and checked against an analytic plane model. The variants cover the brief's control-design items: linearisation and pole maps, controllability/observability rank tests (including the unobservable cases), PID tuning by pole placement with a time-scheduled gain table and step responses with/without a disturbance moment, and the effect of estimation + actuation delay on the closed loop.

All plots here are analysis-only (no trajectory). The nonlinear flights that use these gains are in the Control, Path-following and Robustness demos.

variants.notes:
The 13-state nonlinear model is linearised by central differences through gnc.dynamics.derivatives at 9 points between rail exit (0.37 s) and the start of the thrust tail-off (TVC end, 3.97 s). The attitude error is a body-frame rotation vector, so the quaternion norm constraint never enters; expressing dp, dv in body axes splits the 12-state model into two identical 4-state planes (pitch [z_b, w, theta, q], yaw mirror image), with cross-coupling < 2e-4. The numeric Jacobian matches the analytic plane model to ~1e-10.
Open loop: a lightly damped short-period pair (weathercock oscillation) whose frequency rises with dynamic pressure, a weakly unstable real 'drift' mode (thrusting weathercock divergence, fastest at low speed) and a zero root (lateral position). Closed loop (pole-placement PID on theta): every pole moves into the left half-plane except lateral position, which the guidance loop closes.

variants.notes:
Kalman rank tests (singular-value tolerance 1e-8 relative) with condition numbers of the block-scaled Kalman matrices (each A^k B block normalised, so |A|^k growth does not mask rank). Pitch plane: controllable from delta_p at every point, but the condition number grows by more than an order of magnitude over the boost: the TVC has to beat a stiffening airframe. Gyro, attitude or GPS-velocity outputs alone leave lateral position z_b unobservable (rank 3); GPS position makes the plane fully observable.
Structural losses in the 12-state model: roll angle and roll rate cannot be controlled by a single gimbal, and along-track position is uncontrollable because the motor cannot be throttled. For the observers: GPS position or baro make [p, v, b_a] observable, GPS velocity alone leaves position unobservable, and the accelerometer alone gives pure dead reckoning (rank 0). The attitude estimator [theta, b_gyro] needs an attitude reference (magnetometer). With the gyro alone the bias is unobservable, so the rail-averaged gyro bias and the magnetometer correction are both needed.

variants.notes:
Per operating point the short-period reduction theta'' + a1 theta' + a0 theta = b delta is closed with delta = Kp e + Ki int(e) - Kd q_gyro. Matching s^3 + (a1 + b Kd) s^2 + (a0 + b Kp) s + b Ki to (s + p)(s^2 + 2 zeta wn s + wn^2) gives the gains in closed form (gnc.pid.place_pid). The 'achieved' column is the root set of the resulting characteristic polynomial. The last column closes the same gains around the full 4-state plane, including the drift mode. The dominant pair stays close to the design, and the integrator merges with the stabilised drift mode into slow, well-damped poles.
Step responses: derivative-on-measurement and the PI zero shape the response. The servo lag adds a little overshoot over the 2nd-order spec. A step disturbance moment (equivalent to a 0.5 deg thrust misalignment) is fully trimmed out by the integral action. Without it (PD only, same Kp, Kd) a steady-state error d/(a0 + b Kp) remains. At the end of the boost the same 1 deg step would need a peak gimbal well above the 5 deg limit (linear model). There the TVC can only trim, not manoeuvre.

variants.notes:
Actuation delay (command transport) and estimation delay (sensor samples arriving late) multiply the same single loop by e^{-s tau}, so they are analysed together as the loop delay tau = tau_act + tau_est (Pade approximant). The delay margin is tightest at the end of the boost, where the design bandwidth wn is highest. The pole-migration plot shows the dominant pair travelling right as the delay grows and crossing the imaginary axis at the critical delay.
In the 6-DOF sim the loop also contains ~6 ms of intrinsic delay (10 ms controller sample-and-hold ~5 ms, plus the 1 ms integration step), on top of the configured delays. The 15 + 15 ms case (~36 ms in total) sits just under the mid-boost margin and only touches the end-of-boost margin in the last few tenths of a second. 30 + 30 ms (~66 ms) exceeds the margin everywhere (see the 'Control' demo).
